answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before transacting, so creating many fake identities multiplies the attacker's cost while honest agents earn it back through reliable work. Reputation then grows like a walnut tree, slow and rooted and hard to fake, and any sharp delta in behavior, such as a sudden spike in volume or a shift in counterparties, triggers a review that freezes the stake. Honest activity leaves a consistent echo across counterparties' records, while sock-puppet clusters produce identical hollow patterns that stand out.
